APR 28 2025 REY C. VILLACAMPA Punong Barangay Barangay Bonawon Municipality of Siaton, Province of Negros Oriental Dear Punong Barangay Villacampa: This has reference to your email dated 31 January 2025 wherein you furnished this Department a copy of the Barangay Resolution No. 02-2025 entitled "A RESOLUTION REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DILG) TO PROVIDE A LEGAL OPINION ON WHO IS THE RIGHTFUL OR AUTHORIZED ENTITY TO CONDUCT BARANGAY EVENTS OR ACTIVITIES DURING THE BARANGAY AND SITIO FIESTA." Based on the context of your request, the following legal inquiries have been raised: l. Who is the rightful or authorized individual or entity to conduct barangay events or activities during the barangay fiesta? 2. What guidelines, if any, govern the organization and funding of such activities? 3. Are there specific regulations or directives that delineate the roles and responsibilities of barangay officials, the Sangguniang Kabataan, and other community sectors in the organization of these events? per your representation, there has been confusion concerning the authority to conduct barangay activities, particularly between Barangay Bonawon and the Municipality of Siaton. The Municipality of Siaton has organized activities for the barangay and sitio fiesta that are comparable to those typically conducted by your office. However, these activities were conducted without the approval or consent of Barangay Bonawon officials. In light of this situation, and to resolve the uncertainty regarding the matter, you have deemed it necessary to seek the Department's legal opinion on who holds the legitimate authority to organize and carry out barangay events or activities during the Barangay and Sitio Fiesta. Furthermore, attached to your submission is a copy of an Executive Order issued by the Municipal Mayor of Siaton. The Order, among other provisions, imposes restrictions on the use of the multi-purpose gymnasium located on the land owned by the Municipality of Siaton (as described in Tax Declaration No. 2017-15-0007-00224). Notably, the Order forbids Barangay Bonawon officials and their representatives from using the gymnasium for any purpose, including fiesta-related activities, unless written consent is obtained from Mr. Hernion G. Sojor, the designated caretaker of the property. The Order also entrusts "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Tel. (02) 8876-3454

Mr. Sojor the authority to manage and organize the upcoming fiesta activities, including overseeing the use of the gymnasium for any related events. Upon careful review, it is the understanding of this Level that the central issues to be addressed concern not only the determination of the rightful entity to organize barangay- level activities during the fiesta, but also the propriety of the Executive Order that prohibits certain Barangay Bonawon officials from using the gymnasium for fiesta activities. It is important to note at the outset that this Department, as part of the executive branch of the government, is devoid of authority to declare executive or legislative actions by the local government officials invalid or illegal, even when such actions are alleged to be in contravention of the Local Government Code (the Code) or other relevant laws. Any disputes over the legality of such actions must be resolved and threshed out in the appropriate legal forum. Nevertheless, for the purpose of providing guidance and in accordance with the DILG Secretary's delegated general supervisory authority over local government units and their officials, we shall herein discuss the relevant provisions of the law that we deem applicable to the subject issue. Foremost, we invite your attention to the pertinent provisions of the Code regarding the Accountability and Responsibility for Proper Use and Care of Government Property, viz: "Section 375. Primary and Secondary Accountability for Government Property. — (a) Each head of department or office of a province, city, municipality or barangay shall be primarily accountable for all government property assigned or issued to his department or office. The person or persons entrusted with the possession or custody of government property under the accountability of any head of department or office shall be immediately accountable to such officer. x x x' 'Section 376. Responsibility for Proper Use and Care of Government Property. - The person in actual physical possession of government property or entrusted with its custody and control shall be responsible for its proper use and care and shall exercise due diligence in the utilization and safekeeping thereof." Correlatively, the case of Hermes Frias, Sr. v. People' affirms that municipal mayors, as chief executives of their respective municipalities, are the accountable public officers for all government funds and property under their jurisdiction. Applying these principles to the case at hand, the Municipal Mayor of Siaton, as the primary custodian of government property, is responsible for ensuring its proper use and care. By designating Mr. Sojor as the caretaker of the gymnasium and the land on which it is situated, the Mayor has entrusted Mr. Sojor the duty to exercise due diligence in the I G.R. No. 171437, October 4, 2007. Page 2 of 3

utilization and safekeeping of the property. Therefore, it is our view that the Executive Order issued by the Municipal Mayor of Siaton falls within the bounds of the Code and should be presumed valid unless proven otherwise in court. Nonetheless, should there be any challenge to the Executive Order's validity, the same should be made through a special civil action for Declaratory Relief in the proper legal forum. As regards the query on who is authorized to organize events or activities during the barangay or sitio fiesta, it is our humble opinion that any individual, entity or organization may organize or conduct such an event, provided that the activity is lawful, complies with existing laws, local ordinances, rules, and regulations, and is coordinated with the barangay where the event is being held. Further, as a matter of local courtesy, the barangay, being the local government unit directly governing its territorial jurisdiction, should be consulted to ensure that the event does not conflict with other planned activities and aligns with community interests and welfare. For the other issues raised, you may refer to the relevant provisions of the Code, including but not limited to the provisions under Title V — Local Fiscal Administration, Chapter I General Provisions; and Chapter III Budgeting — Article II (Barangay Budgets). Additionally, the COA Circular No. 2012-0033, may also provide helpful guidance on measures to prevent disallowable expenditures. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to contrary opinion or ruling which may be rendered by competent authorities and the proper courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/drm Copy Furnished: DIR. LEOCADIO T.
